section_summary: This section covers early post-war educational reform in occupied Japan between March 1945 and February 1946, centering on directives issued by the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP) to eliminate militarism and ultra-nationalism from schools. It includes diplomatic despatches and detailed memoranda by Dr. Karl C. Leebrick reporting on SCAP orders regarding textbook revision, educator screening, the restoration of religious freedom at Christian mission schools like Rikkyo Gakuin, and field observations of war damage and conditions across regional Japanese institutions. In addition, the file documents Japanese responses to these reforms, featuring press commentary, historical analysis of state control by Eiichi Nishizawa, rising student activism, inquiries from Nisei teachers, and evaluations of Japanese scientists.

subfiles.about: Memorandum surveying SCAP educational directives, Japanese government cooperation, student strikes, Christian school surveys, and press reactions regarding educational reform.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum by Karl C. Leebrick reviewing SCAP directives on Japanese education, including the elimination of militarism, screening of educators, and restoration of religious freedom at Christian mission schools like Rikkyo Gakuin. It notes apparent cooperation by the Ministry of Education, rising student activism across universities, and widespread public debate on democratic educational reform.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Educational Affairs in Japan, October 1 to November 8, 1945

subfiles.about: SCAP directive ordering the elimination of militarism, revision of curricula and textbooks, screening and reinstatement of teachers, and establishment of democratic educational principles.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: SCAP directive ordering the Japanese Government to eliminate militarism from education, revise curricula and textbooks, screen educational personnel, and institute democratic practices.
subfiles.title: SCAP Directive AG 350 (22 Oct 45) CIE: Administration of the Educational System of Japan

subfiles.about: SCAP directive ordering the dismissal of militarist officials at Rikkyo Gakuin and mandating a comprehensive survey of Christian mission schools throughout Japan.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: SCAP directive ordering the immediate dismissal of Rikkyo Gakuin officials who suppressed Christianity and committed vandalism during the war, barring them from future educational or religious posts. It instructs the Japanese Government to reorganize the university under its Christian charter and conduct a nationwide survey of all institutions founded by foreign Christian missions.
subfiles.title: SCAP Directive AG 000.3 (24 Oct 45) CIS: Violation of Religious Freedom

subfiles.about: SCAP directive instructing the Japanese Government to establish administrative machinery to screen, remove, and bar militarist and demobilized personnel from the educational system.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: SCAP directive instructing the Japanese Ministry of Education to establish administrative machinery to screen and disqualify militaristic, ultra-nationalistic, and demobilized military personnel from teaching.
subfiles.title: SCAP Directive AG 350 (30 Oct 45) CIE: Investigation, Screening, and Certification of Teachers and Educational Officials

subfiles.title: Cover Sheet: Enclosure No. 4 to Despatch No. 49

subfiles.about: Three-part historical analysis examining bureaucratic control, state nationalism, and military drill in Japanese education from the Meiji era to World War II.
subfiles.summary: A three-part article by Eiichi Nishizawa in the Nippon Times examining the history of modern Japanese education from the Meiji Restoration onward. It criticizes excessive government centralization and military drill under Education Minister Yurei Mori, contrasting this with earlier American-inspired reforms and Prince Saionji's liberal policies. The author urges sweeping reforms to eliminate bureaucracy and cultivate democratic initiative.
subfiles.title: Newspaper Article Series: Education in the Past Marked by Government Interference

subfiles.about: Memorandum surveying Japanese Ministry of Education actions, textbook suspensions, coeducation initiatives, student strikes, and teacher union organizing.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum by Karl C. Leebrick reporting on Japanese educational developments between November 9 and December 1, 1945. It details Ministry of Education measures including the discontinuance of military training, coeducation in higher schools, textbook printing suspensions, and principal reassignments. The report also highlights widespread student unrest, debates over imperial portraits, and the formation of a democratic teachers' union.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Educational Affairs in Japan, November 9 to December 1, 1945
